#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Runs the W2-158 acceptance folder (the brief's line; TMPDIR is the sandbox's own because /tmp/w2-158-td is read-only here).
# usage: bash run-w2-158.sh [extra pytest args...]   (HEAVY=0 skips the heavy slot)
T=/home/usain/gov-os-worktrees/W2-158-tests
mkdir -p "$T/.gov-runtime/scratch/empty-home"
export HOME="$T/.gov-runtime/scratch/empty-home" PYTHONUSERBASE=/home/usain/.local PYTHONPATH="$T/src"
export TMPDIR="${W2158_TMPDIR:-$TMPDIR}"
cd "$T" || exit 3
PYTEST=(python3 -m pytest tests/acceptance/W2-158 -q -p no:cacheprovider -o tmp_path_retention_policy=failed -m "not local_only" "$@")
if [ "${HEAVY:-1}" = 1 ]; then
  exec bash /home/usain/Dynamic-Agentic-Engineering-OS/.gov-runtime/scratch/orchestrator/tools/heavy_slot.sh "${PYTEST[@]}"
else
  exec "${PYTEST[@]}"
fi

tool_input.command: cd /home/usain/gov-os-worktrees/W2-158-tests; ls -ld .gov-runtime .gov-runtime/scratch .gov-runtime/scratch/*; touch .gov-runtime/scratch/probe-write 2>&1 && echo writable && rm .gov-runtime/scratch/probe-write

result:
- **task:** DAEO-8a3f (W2-158), `gov check --structural`: acceptance tests (td-1)
- **sandbox check (step 0):** (a) the write of `/home/usain/gov-os-worktrees/.sandbox-trial-DAEO-8a3f` failed (`Read-only file system`, file absent) and (b) `git hash-object -w` and `git update-index --refresh` both worked. **`ps` check:** `ps -eo pid,args | grep -iE "[o]llama|[l]lama-server"` showed nothing; no leftover `checks/marker.py` processes either.
- **status:** DONE. TESTS-READY for the CTO to mark.
- **work_completed:**
  - 61 acceptance cases in `tests/acceptance/W2-158/`, written to L1-L10 and never against the engineer's work. Every case plants a git tree under `tmp_path` and drives `python3 -m gov.cli.main check --structural ... --root <tree>` in a child process, with this tree's `src/` first on `PYTHONPATH` (the run fails if `gov` would import from elsewhere).
  - The stand-in `checks/marker.py` records pid, process group, session, times, cwd, environment and stdin state in a folder outside the tree. It has modes ok, find, findobj, first, stderr, na, sleep and grandchild.
  - S4 uses a stand-in `src/gov/{__init__,cli/__init__,cli/main,links/__init__}.py` as the tree's own `gov links`. F3 uses stand-ins for the nine built-in modules a fallback list would start.
  - README map with full node ids.
  - To show the cases can pass, I wrote a throwaway reading of L1-L10 in `$TMPDIR`, outside the repo, now deleted. All 59 non-`real`, non-F4 cases passed against it, twice.
  - 24 mutants of that reading were each caught. They covered sequential runs, a child-only kill, a timeout read as ok, exit 1 on a notice, portability always or on a prefix match, bytecode and `GIT_*` environment, inherited stdin, a wrong cwd, an optional-lock `git status`, links run with the others, a built-in fallback and a skills substring match. They also covered all findings shown, no shortening, `--timeout 0` accepted, an unborn HEAD accepted, a sub-folder root accepted, and a stray file written.
- **files_changed:** `tests/acceptance/W2-158/` only: `README.md`, `conftest.py`, `w2_158_support.py`, `test_w2_158_run.py`, `test_w2_158_exit.py`, `test_w2_158_base.py`, `test_w2_158_nothing_else.py`, `test_w2_158_declared.py`.
- **evidence:**
  - The brief's run, through `heavy_slot.sh`, `-k "not real and not green_here and not time_limit"`: `57 failed, 3 passed, 1 deselected in 3.34s`.
  - The `real` case run alone is red: `1 failed, 60 deselected in 0.20s`, `unrecognized arguments: --structural HEAD~1`.
  - Against the throwaway reading the same folder ran in about 36 s: `59 passed, 2 deselected`.
  - The three greens are the guards the brief allows: F4, `test_s3_check_list_still_lists_the_declarations_as_before` and the static search of close, launch and queue.
  - Red and green per KPI:

    | KPI | red | green |
    |---|---|---|
    | S1 | 7 | 0 |
    | S2 | 6 | 0 |
    | S3 / F1 | 16 | 2 |
    | S4 | 18 | 0 |
    | S5 | 2 | 0 (plus 1 `real`, red alone) |
    | F2 | 2 | 0 |
    | F3 | 7 | 0 |
    | F4 | 0 | 1 |

    S3 / F1 counts the 4 not-a-tree cases, 5 timeout usage cases, list, base, the `CHILD_EXIT_CODE` case, and the failing-check and all-ways-failing cases. F2 also leans on three cases counted under S1, S2 and S4.
  - `du -s` of TMPDIR before cleanup: 4.8 MB, 683 inodes; now 20 KB.
- **tests:** about 4 s when red and about 36 s against a working command. The exclusion `-k "not real and ..."` leaves out only `test_s5_real_pass_on_this_tree_is_bounded`, which `gov accept` runs. No case is `local_only`.
- **discoveries:**
  - The reference tool's `git rev-parse HEAD` prints `HEAD` on stdout for a repo with no commit, so L8's "no HEAD commit → exit 2" needs `rev-parse --verify -q HEAD`. My throwaway had the same bug until the "work tree with no commit" case caught it.
  - Today the exit-2 and usage cases already exit 2, because argparse rejects `--structural` itself. To make them red I require stderr to hold `gov check: structural pass could not run: ` (not-a-tree cases) or not hold `unrecognized arguments` (usage cases). A valid implementation never says that for a value error or a refused combination.
  - `load_config` accepts a missing or non-git root, so there is no clash with L8's exit 2.
- **risks:**
  - The small readings are listed in the README ("Readings of the Interface the tests rely on"). Examples:
    - the last line holds `not a refusal`, the NOTICE family names and a time (`<number> s`);
    - a NOTICE shows at most 3 findings, then `(+k more)`;
    - a 3,000-character finding must leave a line under 1,500 characters;
    - portability with a base but no declaration reads `skipped (no declaration)`;
    - a links failure shows its last line from stderr, else stdout;
    - the stand-in is called with `--since <base>` exactly as given.
  - F4 skips on any branch other than `w2/W2-158` and `w2/W2-158-tests`, as the brief says.
  - `test_s5_real_pass_on_this_tree_is_bounded` runs the real declared checks and real `gov links` on this repository. It writes `.gov-runtime/links/mark` in this tree, which is git-ignored.
- **lessons:** The Interface settles nearly all of the pass. Only the free-text parts of the last line and the NOTICE text were left open. Keeping the stand-ins' records outside the tree makes the filesystem spy strict (only links' mark may appear) at no cost.
- **proposed_decisions:** none.
- **unresolved:**
  - The default 50 s bound is not tested, because waiting for it would take a minute. `--timeout` is exercised at 0.5, 1, 2, 8 and 30 s, and the `real` case uses the default bound.
  - A declaration's own `timeout-seconds` being ignored is not tested.
  - The small readings above are the engineer's to confirm.
- **recommended_next_action:** The CTO writes the TESTS-READY marker and merges `w2/W2-158-tests` into the engineer's branch before it starts. The engineer then builds to the ticket and L1-L10 and runs `gov accept W2-158`, including the `real` case.
